summary: UC Berkeley applied AI engineer with a foundation in machine learning and deep learning, plus hands-on Python, PyTorch, TensorFlow, AWS, and full-stack product delivery. Built and evaluated reliable AI systems: reduced LLM-agent benchmarking cost by 63% at SAIL, improved ITSM-agent reliability to 95% at Zendesk, and reduced enterprise retrieval time by 85% at Prologis. Brings rigorous evaluation, data-system integration, and workflow design to applied AI products.

bullets: Led development of an enterprise RAG platform integrating Dataiku, Snowflake, and OpenAI for citation-backed querying.
Designed product workflows for unified qualitative and quantitative search, improving access to two retrieval engines.
Consolidated 1,000+ fragmented documents into a scalable knowledge system, reducing information-retrieval time by 85%.
Designed an adaptive evaluation framework for LLM agents, reducing benchmarking cost by 63% through statistical guiding.
Benchmarked 20+ cold-start prompt strategies across WebArena tasks and identified high-performing configurations 3x faster.
Implemented adaptive resource allocation that reduced evaluation runtime by 32% by prioritizing informative evaluations.
Improved reliability to 95% by designing and benchmarking ITSM-agent architectures for uncertain tasks.
Evaluated 100+ tickets by building frameworks that measured reasoning quality, hallucinations, and action accuracy.
Reduced hallucinations and unsafe tool use by about 27% through evidence-based capability firewalls and mitigation systems.
Developed multi-stage LLM analysis with sub-two-second transcript retrieval from long-form videos through indexing.
Reduced repeat-access latency by about 95% using Redis caching, Celery task orchestration, and WebSocket streams.
